our_interpretation: We read 'price increases on AI-native companies' as increases in what model providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic charge companies that build products on their models, because the surrounding sentences discuss those two providers. The sentence itself does not say who raises prices.
We do not assign an end date to 'the next few months'. The speaker gave none.
criteria.support_condition: Model providers raised the prices they charge AI-native companies at least twice within a few months after 2025-10-20.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No model provider raised the prices it charges AI-native companies within a few months after 2025-10-20.

payload.rationale: Zitron wrote on 2025-10-20 that he believed there would be multiple price increases on AI-native companies in the next few months. This is an unqualified forecast, but it gives no end date, does not say who would raise prices, and does not define a price increase. Which evidence would count depends on an end date and a definition that he did not give. We did not collect price-change evidence, so the record is unresolved.
limitations: This record does not assess whether model providers changed their prices after October 2025.
Reading the price-setters as model providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic comes from the surrounding sentences, not from the sentence itself.
payload.what_would_resolve: A stated end date for 'the next few months' and a stated definition of a price increase on an AI-native company.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent tests published late in 2025 show general-purpose agents completing most realistic multi-step work tasks across broad uses, or agents were not prominently promoted during 2025.

payload.rationale: On January 1, 2025, under 'High confidence', Marcus predicted that AI agents would be endlessly hyped throughout 2025 but far from reliable, except possibly in very narrow use cases. OpenAI promoted agents in January, June, and October 2025, from saying they may 'join the workforce' to launching tools to build them. Independent benchmarks found the best agent completed 30% of simulated workplace tasks (September 2025) and 2.5% of real remote-work projects (30 October 2025).
limitations: The promotion shown comes from one company, OpenAI. It does not measure how much agents were promoted across the industry.
Both benchmarks are preprints, and the latest is from 30 October 2025, not the end of the year.
Whether an agent use counts as a 'very narrow use case' is not defined by the speaker.
